podcast.title: Disbandment Due to Monkhood
podcast.body: The band broke up when their guitarist made the decision to become a Hare Krishna monk, an event that effectively destroyed their momentum and plans. At the time, they had already written material for what was intended to be their second album, which they planned to title "Rage Against The Machine." "See, their guitars decided to become a Harry Christian monk, and that kind of destroyed everything."

podcast.title: National Underground Following
podcast.body: Inside Out successfully cultivated a considerable following within the National Underground Hardcore scene, achieving particular success and recognition in the Orange County area and its surroundings. "They were actually able to get a decent following on the National Underground Hardcore scene, and did especially well in and around Orange County."

xref.title: First Zero-G Music Video (2014)
xref.body: OK Go partnered with Russian airline S7 to produce the first-ever Zero-G music video for their song "Upside Down and Inside Out." The video was filmed by flying a plane through a series of extreme parabolic trajectories, creating momentary periods of zero gravity. While Commander Chris Hadfield filmed a Zero-G video in space in 2013, OK Go's video is recognized for being filmed within the Earth's atmosphere. "Ok go teamed with a Russian airline called S7 to create the first ever Zero-G Music video for a song called Upside Down and Inside Out."

xref.title: Band Naming
xref.body: The band adopted the name "Rage Against The Machine" from the title of a planned second album by Zach Dela Roka's previous band, Inside Out, which never materialized. The name was ultimately deemed more fitting and powerful for the new group. "the band had decided that Rage against the machine would be a great name."
